question.text: Fund LMN holds: LONG 2 lakh shares Company C at INR 250, SHORT 2 lakh shares Company D at INR 500, LONG 1 lakh mid-cap E at INR 500, SHORT 1.5 lakh mid-cap F at INR 500. Large-cap net: -INR 5 cr; Mid-cap net: -INR 2.5 cr. This is:

explanation.text: The Logic: Both sector sub-books are NET SHORT (large-cap -5 cr, mid-cap -2.5 cr). Per Section 10.1.1.4 and Example 10.4 Fund LMN, this is a Short-bias Directional Strategy. The Trap: A is net long. C requires ~ zero net. D needs a corporate event. Cross-Exam Context: PDF Example 10.4 verbatim. XIX-C same. Manager's Pro-Tip: Short-bias with INR 7.5 cr net short on smaller NAV funds can still be within risk limits IF the short leg is diversified across sectors. Concentrated single-sector shorts (like financials only) carry gamma risk on takeouts and dividends.
